classification.difficultyReason: Choose compatible subdivisions, convert improper and mixed forms as needed, and translate the values into positions on a constructed number line.

content.prompt: Draw a number line marked with the whole numbers from 0 to 3, and indicate on it where the markers for $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{4}{2}$, $\frac{3}{4}$, $1\frac{3}{8}$ and $\frac{19}{8}$ are located.

answer.worked:
Divide each unit interval into eight equal parts. Use the equivalent forms below to position the markers.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{1}{2}&=\frac{4}{8}\\\frac{4}{2}&=2\\\frac{3}{4}&=\frac{6}{8}\\1\frac{3}{8}&=\frac{11}{8}\\\frac{19}{8}&=2\frac{3}{8}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Complete solution number line with integer labels from 0 to 3, eighth-unit subdivisions and all five requested fraction markers.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer editions only; the student draws the entire number line.
